Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning
summary_zh: 引入概率偏差校正，提高亚季节预测的准确性。实验表明，该框架有效减少系统误差。
summary_en: Introduces probabilistic bias correction to advance subseasonal forecasting accuracy. Experiments show that this framework effectively reduces systematic error.
insights: 创新点：提出概率偏差校正，提高亚季节预测。
方法亮点：学习校正历史概率预测。
关键发现：有效减少系统误差。
insights_en: Novelty: Introduces probabilistic bias correction to improve subseasonal forecasting.
Method highlight: Learns to correct historical probabilistic forecasts.
Key finding: Effectively reduces systematic error.
abstract: Decision-makers rely on weather forecasts to plant crops, manage wildfires, allocate water and energy and prepare for weather extremes1–3. Today, such forecasts enjoy unprecedented accuracy as far as 2 weeks thanks to steady advances in physics-based dynamical models and data-driven artificial intelligence models4–10. However, model skill drops precipitously at subseasonal timescales (2–6 weeks ahead) due to compounding errors, systemic model biases and the chaotic nature of the atmosphere11–15. To counter this degradation, we introduce probabilistic bias correction, a machine learning framework that substantially reduces systematic error by learning to correct historical probabilistic forecasts. When applied to the leading dynamical and artificial intelligence models from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), probabilistic bias correction doubles the modest subseasonal skill of the AI Forecasting System16 and improves the skill of the operationally debiased dynamical model17 for 91% of pressure, 92% of temperature and 98% of precipitation targets. We designed probabilistic bias correction for operational deployment, and, in the 2025 real-time forecasting competition of ECMWF18, its global forecasts were the best for all weather variables and lead times, outperforming the dynamical models from six operational forecasting centres, an international dynamical multimodel ensemble, the AI Forecasting System of ECMWF and the forecasting systems of 34 teams worldwide. These probabilistic skill gains translate into more accurate prediction of extreme events and have the potential to improve agricultural planning, energy management and disaster preparedness in vulnerable communities19. The AI framework probabilistic bias correction is shown to correct weather forecast errors 2 to 6 weeks ahead and boost forecast skill, making it promising for improved extreme-weather prediction.

title: Global conservation area coverage substantially exceeds current estimates
summary_zh: 全球保护区覆盖面积远超现有估计。研究显示，保护区覆盖面积可能增加。
summary_en: Global conservation area coverage substantially exceeds current estimates. The study shows that conservation area coverage may increase.
insights: 创新点：评估全球保护区覆盖面积。
方法亮点：使用全球代表性样本。
关键发现：保护区覆盖面积可能增加。
insights_en: Novelty: Evaluates global conservation area coverage.
Method highlight: Uses a globally representative sample.
Key finding: Conservation area coverage may increase.
abstract: Conservation areas are critical for tackling the global environmental crisis1. These sites are reported as covering 18.5% of the terrestrial realm2 and governments have committed through Global Biodiversity Framework Target 3 to increase this to at least 30% by 2030 (ref. 3). There are concerns that this potential near-doubling of conservation area coverage will negatively affect vulnerable people and over-stretch conservation resources4. However, nationally available datasets indicate that more conservation areas exist than are reflected in global figures5–7. We evaluated progress towards the area component of Target 3 using a globally representative sample across 25 countries and territories that incorporated these national datasets8. Extrapolating from this sample, we show that conservation areas likely already cover 26.81% of the terrestrial realm. We may be much closer to achieving 30% terrestrial coverage than previously thought. However, we also show that the extra land does not substantially address gaps in ecological representativeness, indicating that solely meeting the area component of Target 3 will do little to solve continuing global biodiversity loss. More focus and resources are needed to achieve the other components of the target, using a more strategic and inclusive approach to fill present gaps and produce equitable and effective conservation area networks. A globally representative sample of 25 countries and territories indicates that conservation areas cover 26.81% of the land, much closer to the 30% by 2030 target than officially reported.
